title: Huntington Disease
subject: Biochemistry & genetics
summary: Huntington disease is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by CAG repeat expansion in HTT. It presents with chorea, cognitive decline and psychiatric symptoms, progressing over decades.

sections.p: Huntington disease (HD) is a hereditary movement disorder with a classic triad of chorea, cognitive decline and psychiatric disturbance. Onset is usually in mid‑30s to 50s, but juvenile forms exist.

The expanded polyglutamine tract in huntingtin protein leads to misfolding, aggregation and neuronal death, especially in the caudate and putamen. This disrupts basal ganglia circuits, producing hyperkinetic movements.
No disease‑modifying therapy exists. Management focuses on symptom control and supportive care. Genetic counselling is essential for families.

Neuronal loss in the striatum causes disinhibition of thalamocortical pathways, leading to chorea. Cortical involvement produces executive dysfunction and dementia. Psychiatric symptoms arise from limbic system changes.
b: Cognitive decline – executive dysfunction, memory loss

sections.p: In low‑resource settings, HD may be misdiagnosed as psychiatric illness or infectious encephalitis. Early recognition prevents unnecessary investigations and allows timely counselling.
b: History of progressive movement and mood changes

t.b: Confirms autosomal dominant pattern; absence suggests sporadic or other disorders
Positive if >39 repeats; confirms diagnosis when clinical picture is unclear
Shows caudate atrophy and hyperintensity; useful when genetic testing unavailable

sections.p: Treat the underlying psychiatric and movement symptoms with supportive care. Avoid drugs that worsen chorea or cause hepatotoxicity.

t.b: Reduce chorea; monitor for anticholinergic toxicity
Alleviate anxiety and chorea; avoid in severe hepatic impairment

sections.p: Differential includes Wilson disease, neuroacanthocytosis, chorea-acanthocytosis, and infectious encephalitis.
b: Wilson disease – low ceruloplasmin, Kayser‑Fleischer rings

sections.p: Normal MRI does not exclude early HD; CAG repeat testing may be unavailable. Psychiatric symptoms can be misattributed to primary psychiatric disorders.
Remember the classic triad, autosomal dominant inheritance, and CAG repeat expansion. In exam questions, focus on distinguishing features from Wilson disease and infectious causes.
Urgent referral if patient shows severe agitation, self‑harm, or rapid neurological decline.

faq.a: It is autosomal dominant; each child of an affected person has a 50% chance of inheriting the mutant allele.

faq.q: What is the diagnostic test for HD?
faq.a: PCR for CAG repeat length in the HTT gene; >39 repeats confirms disease.
No cure exists; treatment is symptomatic and supportive, with genetic counselling for families.

exam: A 35‑year‑old man presents with involuntary movements and mood swings. What is the most likely diagnosis? — Huntington disease (triad of chorea, cognitive decline, psychiatric symptoms).
You suspect Huntington disease but the patient has low ceruloplasmin and Kayser‑Fleischer rings. What is the next step? — Diagnose Wilson disease; order serum copper and urinary copper.
A patient with confirmed HD develops severe depression. Which drug is safest? — Atypical antipsychotic (e.g., risperidone) with low hepatotoxicity.
You have a patient with chorea but normal MRI and no family history. What should you do? — Repeat CAG repeat testing; consider other causes like Wilson disease, neuroacanthocytosis.
A 28‑year‑old woman with juvenile HD presents with seizures. What is the most likely cause? — Seizures are common in juvenile HD due to cortical involvement.

You are in a rural clinic with no genetic testing. A patient shows classic HD features. What is your management plan? — Provide supportive care, refer for genetic counselling, treat psychiatric symptoms, monitor for complications.
A patient with HD is on haloperidol but develops extrapyramidal symptoms. What is the alternative? — Switch to risperidone or olanzapine, which have lower EPS risk.
